label: IN_ACT_FORMALLY_1: A cause is IN_ACT_FORMALLY_1 in a perfection when it has that perfection in the…
definition: A cause is in act formally in a perfection when it has that perfection in the same form in which it produces it, as fire that is hot makes the wood hot.
note: Lean: a primitive parameter of the sense-fork frame (its own declaration, distinct from the other senses of its disambiguation); it carries no definitional body.

formal_gap.meaning: ActFrame.InActFormally x r says that x has the perfection r in the same form in which it produces it in another, as fire that is hot makes wood hot. It is a supplied relation between a being and a respect: the formal (univocal) sense of 'in act' (DISAMB-IN-ACT).
examples: Hot fire heating wood, with r being hot.
exclusions: Having r only virtually or eminently, as a power to produce it without having it in the same form (InActVirtually).
open_obligations: Its relation to InActVirtually and to the shared InAct (DEF-ACT) is fixed only by the fork's open premises; formal act is not assumed to imply virtual act or conversely.
Non-simultaneity with InPotency is an explicit premise in each sense, not a law of the field.
No formalization candidate from existing vocabulary.
